name: Wroclaw University of Science and Technology
summary: Wrocław technical university with 21,000 students, 1,300 international; five English-taught bachelor's in computing, engineering and management.

ib.text: IB grades become an admission index: Maths plus one extra subject (HL counts 2.5 times SL) and 0.1 of English. The Diploma covers B2 English. Every foreign candidate sits an online maths-and-logic exam.

programmes.name: Applied Computer Science
programmes.about: A seven-semester computing engineering degree: programming, algorithms, databases, networks, IoT, cybersecurity, cloud and AI, on a base of maths and physics; a team project replaces the individual engineering thesis.
programmes.overview: Subjects include software development with programming languages and techniques, algorithms and data structures, computer networks, databases and data warehouses, mobile, distributed and web systems, multimedia and intelligent IT systems, IT project management, and foundations in physics and mathematics with some management and social communication. The English-taught Computer Engineering specialisation focuses on analysing and modelling complex IT systems, advanced databases and expert systems, parallel and distributed processing and AI-based methods.

Scored as the extra subject (HL x2.5); the programme page also accepts Computer Science

programmes.selectionNote: Ranked on Maths + best of Physics (HL x2.5) + 0.1 English; pass the maths-logic exam. 30 places in 2026. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Management
programmes.about: A six-semester degree in organisational management at a technical university: economics, finance, accounting, marketing, logistics and operations, with data analysis, IT modules and project leadership.
programmes.overview: You study finance and accounting, logistics and production planning, marketing and sales, human resources, business law and intellectual property, mathematical and statistical methods and IT tools. Teaching leans on case studies, workshops and simulations, with team-based projects and mobile management applications. The English-taught Organizational Management specialisation covers strategy, financial management, team leadership and the effect of global trends and digital technology on organisations. Internships take place with firms such as UBS, Credit Suisse and Polish companies in finance and logistics, and graduates become managers, project managers, business analysts, consultants, HR and marketing specialists or founders, in banking, consulting, HR and manufacturing.

programmes.selectionNote: Ranked on Maths + best of Physics (HL x2.5) + 0.1 English; pass the maths-logic exam. 30 places in 2026. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Mechanical Engineering
programmes.about: Machine design and manufacturing, specialising in mechanical engineering design: mechanics, strength of materials, thermodynamics, CAD and finite elements, CNC manufacturing, vehicle and hydraulic drive systems.
programmes.overview: The seven-semester course covers methods of designing devices, the properties and selection of construction materials, modern manufacturing technologies, and technical diagnostics and repair, with mechanical engineering design as the specialisation. Teaching combines laboratory work and projects and ends with a thesis project. Internships and industrial placements are offered with employers such as Bosch, Volkswagen, Toyota, Volvo, Collins Aerospace and KGHM, and around 160 student science circles run alongside. Graduates work as design engineers, process engineers, R&D engineers and operations and maintenance engineers in the vehicle, machinery and equipment sectors.

programmes.selectionNote: Ranked on Maths + best of Physics (HL x2.5) + 0.1 English; pass the maths-logic exam. 20 places in 2026. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Medical Informatics
programmes.about: An engineering degree joining computer science, electronics and medicine: programming, databases and AI alongside anatomy, biophysics, medical imaging and electromedical devices, for building health-care IT systems.
programmes.overview: The seven-semester engineering course is interdisciplinary and looks at biomedical applications of artificial intelligence, big data, mobile and wearable devices, and augmented and virtual reality. You carry out your own research projects and can join one of several student circles. It follows a single track with no named specialisations. Graduates are prepared to work in hospitals and clinical and outpatient units, medical device manufacturing and distribution, research institutions, IT companies and education.

programmes.name: Electronic and Computer Engineering
programmes.about: Electronics combined with programming, machine learning and robotics: electronic circuits, sensors, microcontrollers, telecommunications and automation, for designing embedded, IoT and robotic systems.
programmes.overview: You learn programming in C, C++, C#, Java, Python and assembly, plus embedded systems on FPGAs, design and programming of robotic systems, PLC controllers and measurement systems, analogue and digital electronic design, and the implementation of machine learning and neural network algorithms. Graduates work in electronic systems design and manufacturing, industrial automation and robotics, software development, and research and development centres, in roles such as software developer, DevOps engineer, tester, designer or electronics engineer, and can continue to a second-cycle degree taught in English.

notes: EU/EEA and Swiss citizens take the free-of-charge route (same IRK and dates, upload your EU ID) and pay nothing for full-time English-taught study; ask the admissions office if you do not yet live in Poland.
The online maths-with-logic exam is compulsory for all foreign candidates, IB holders included; you need 30% to pass and must register and pay the fee by the IRK deadline to sit it.
Registration closes before IB results: register with what you have, then upload your results by the document deadline. You may apply to up to six programmes, 100 PLN each.
